### CVE-2026-79704 — Apache bRPC: Out-of-bounds Read in Multi-stream RPC Response Handling
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the streaming RPC client of Apache bRPC (versions 1.11.0 through  1.17.0) on all platforms. A client that creates multiple streams in a single RPC expects the server response to carry exactly one extra_stream_id for every additional stream. The response handling path indexed the returned identifiers using the locally created stream count without first validating the size of the returned list, so a malicious or compromised server (or an on-path attacker) can trigger an out-of-bounds read in the client by returning a malformed StreamSettings response with fewer extra_stream_ids than expected. This may crash the client process (denial of service) or leak unintended memory contents into subsequent stream handling; surplus identifiers have no valid client-stream mapping and are processed inconsistently.

Root Cause:
Since bRPC 1.11.0, a client can create multiple streams in one RPC via batch StreamCreate. The expected behavior is that the server response must return exactly (N-1) extra_stream_ids, where N is the number of locally created streams. In Controller::HandleStreamConnection, the response path reads extra_stream_ids[i-1] for each additional local stream without first comparing the returned list size with (N-1). If the server returns fewer identifiers, the read runs past the end of the returned list (out-of-bounds read); if it returns more, the surplus identifiers have no corresponding client-side stream.

Affected Scenarios:
A bRPC client using multi-stream RPC (creating more than one stream in a single RPC) that connects to an untrusted, malicious, or compromised server or to a server reached through an untrusted network path. The server sends a malformed StreamSettings response to trigger the issue.


How to Fix: 
(Choose one of the following options) 
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3485 


Note:
The fix makes the client reject responses whose extra_stream_ids count does not exactly match the number of additional client streams. Such mismatched responses now fail the RPC with ERESPONSE and go through the existing stream cleanup path, instead of being partially processed.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 1.11.0 <1.18.0 (semver)

Credits: Claude

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread/2pf15ojj0vr7rtx95677kgtl1mx3gdgb [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-79983 — Apache Camel: camel-ftp resolved the remote path of a polled file from the name reported in the server directory listing without constraining it to the directory being polled, so a listing entry containing traversal segments could be moved outside
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-20 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-22 CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Apache Camel FTP component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The Camel remote-file consumers poll a directory on a remote server and build the absolute remote path of each file by concatenating the configured directory with the file name reported in the server's directory listing. That concatenation (FtpUtils.absoluteFilePath and GenericFileConsumer) applied no lexical normalization and no check that the result stayed inside the directory being polled, and the resulting path became the operand for every subsequent remote operation on the file: retrieval (FtpOperations.retrieveFile / SftpOperations, reached from GenericFileConsumer where the retrieve name is taken verbatim from GenericFile.getAbsoluteFilePath), deletion when delete=true (GenericFileDeleteProcessStrategy), and renaming when move, preMove, moveFailed or readLock=rename is configured (GenericFileProcessStrategySupport and GenericFileRenameExclusiveReadLockStrategy). Neither isValidFile nor isMatched performed any containment check. A listing entry that is not a single path segment therefore resolved to a path outside the configured polling directory, causing Camel to read, delete or rename files outside it using the endpoint's own credentials. A listing name is not route-controlled data. It is supplied by the remote server, and the FTP control channel carries no integrity protection at all, so an on-path attacker can rewrite a LIST response without holding any credentials; a compromised, malicious or multi-tenant server, or a server backed by a virtual filesystem, can emit such a name directly. Retrieval is reachable in a default consumer configuration, since the remote consumers download every listed file; deletion and renaming additionally require one of the disposition options above, all of which are common. Escape from the directory Camel was configured to poll is unconditional, while escape from the server's own account boundary additionally depends on whether that server confines the account. The jailStartingDirectory option, which is documented as restricting Camel to the starting directory and is enabled by default, governed producer writes and, since the localWorkDirectory containment work, consumer downloads to the local work directory - but it did not constrain this remote operand, so its name and description claimed a boundary that was not enforced here. The same entry point had already been recognised on the local side: the localWorkDirectory download path was constrained so that a remote file name containing parent-directory segments could not resolve outside the local work directory. The remote operand was the remaining half of that surface. This artifact provides the ftp, ftps and sftp schemes, all of which are affected. The reporter demonstrated the issue end to end against an ftp endpoint, driving a Camel route with a malicious server whose LIST response named a file outside the polled directory.



Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.22.x releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x stream reached end of life and does not receive this fix; users on it should move to a supported releases stream.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, prefer the encrypted transports, sftp or ftps rather than ftp, so that a directory listing cannot be rewritten in transit by an on-path attacker, and verify the server's host key or certificate. Constrain the consumer with the filter, antInclude or include options so that only simple single-segment file names are accepted, and avoid enabling delete=true, move, preMove, moveFailed or readLock=rename on endpoints pointing at a server whose listing content is not fully trusted, since those options are what turn the issue from a read into a destructive operation. Where the server supports it, confine the account used by the endpoint to the polled directory, so that the server itself enforces the boundary independently of Camel. ### CVE-2026-79993 — Apache ZooKeeper: Missing ACL check on deleteContainer opcode allows unauthorized deletion of any empty persistent/container znode
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-16 | Updated: 2026-09-17 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-862 CWE-862 Missing Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

The `deleteContainer` opcode (0x14/20) is processed without verifying the caller's ACL permissions, allowing any authenticated client to delete specific znodes in the data tree regardless of the ACL restrictions on the znode or its parent. This opcode is considered internal-only and the official client doesn't have API for it, but a client that can open a plain TCP session on the ZooKeeper client port (2181 by default) - with NO authentication and NO ACL permissions - can delete any empty persistent znode (including regular persistent nodes, container nodes, and TTL nodes) by issuing the raw protocol OpCode deleteContainer (20). The deleteContainer request path completely skips both the session check and the DELETE ACL check that are enforced by the regular delete (OpCode 2) path. This is an authorization bypass / ACL enforcement bug.

This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper: from 3.9.0 through 3.9.5, from 3.8.0 through 3.8.6.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.9.6 or 3.8.7, which fixes the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache ZooKeeper: affected 3.9.0 <=3.9.5 (maven); affected 3.8.0 <=3.8.6 (maven)

### CVE-2026-80312 — Apache Camel: Camel-OAuth Authentication Bypass via Fail-Open Processors
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-19 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-287 CWE-287 Improper Authentication
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Improper Authentication vulnerability in Apache Camel OAuth component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.11.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The camel-oauth processors that guard a route did not stop the exchange when authentication could not be completed. Where a failure to establish an authenticated session should have terminated routing and returned an error to the caller, the processors fell through and returned control to the route, so the request continued to the protected endpoint as though authentication had succeeded. The effect is a fail-open authentication guard: an unauthenticated caller reached whatever the route did next. The condition is reached on the ordinary request path of a route configured to require OAuth, and needs no special configuration or prior access on the caller's part.



Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The processors now stop the exchange and set the appropriate error status whenever an authenticated session cannot be established, so a failed authentication no longer reaches the protected part of the route. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, place an explicit authorization check after the OAuth processor rather than relying on it to halt the exchange, and verify that the route stops on failure.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, place an explicit authorization check after the OAuth processor rather than relying on it to halt the exchange, and verify that the route stops on failure.

**solutions:** Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The processors now stop the exchange and set the appropriate error status whenever an authenticated session cannot be established, so a failed authentication no longer reaches the protected part of the route.

### CVE-2026-80343 — Apache Camel: Camel-Netty-HTTP Security Constraint Bypass via Case-Sensitive Context-Path Matching
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-19 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-178 CWE-178 Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity vulnerability in Apache Camel Netty HTTP component.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The camel-netty-http security constraint compared the request path against the configured context path using a case-sensitive match, while the routing that dispatches the request to the endpoint did not apply the same rule. The two comparisons therefore disagreed for any path whose case differed from the configured value. An external caller could alter the case of a character in a path segment so that the security constraint no longer recognised the path as protected, while the request still dispatched to the same endpoint. The result is that the constraint is skipped and the protected route is reached without satisfying it. No credential, prior access or special configuration is required beyond being able to send a request to the consumer.



Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The constraint now matches the request path with the same case rules the dispatch uses, so the two can no longer disagree. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, place the authorization decision in front of the Camel consumer, for example in a reverse proxy that normalises the request path before forwarding.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, place the authorization decision in front of the Camel consumer, for example in a reverse proxy that normalises the request path before forwarding.

**solutions:** Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The constraint now matches the request path with the same case rules the dispatch uses, so the two can no longer disagree.

- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Camel: affected 4.0.0 <4.18.5 (maven); affected 4.19.0 <4.22.1 (maven); unaffected 4.18.5 (maven); unaffected 4.22.1 (maven); unaffected 4.23.0 (maven)

### CVE-2026-80344 — Apache Camel: Camel-AS2 Server-Side Request Forgery and Credential Disclosure via Asynchronous MDN Delivery Address
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-19 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Camel AS2 component.

This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.0.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.

In the AS2 protocol the sender of a message may request that the Message Disposition Notification be returned asynchronously to an address the sender supplies. camel-as2 took that address from the inbound message and used it as the destination for the outgoing receipt without constraining it to anything the deployment had configured. A remote partner therefore chose the host the Camel instance would connect to when delivering the MDN. That gives server-side request forgery from the position of the AS2 receiver, including reaching hosts that are only routable from inside the deployment's network, and where the outbound connection carries credentials configured for MDN delivery those credentials are presented to the attacker-chosen destination.

Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The asynchronous MDN destination is now constrained rather than taken verbatim from the inbound message. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, restrict outbound connectivity from the AS2 receiver to the partner endpoints it legitimately delivers receipts to, and do not attach credentials to MDN delivery that are valid for any host other than those partners.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, restrict outbound connectivity from the AS2 receiver to the partner endpoints it legitimately delivers receipts to, and do not attach credentials to MDN delivery that are valid for any host other than those partners.

**solutions:** Upgrade to Apache Camel 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. Users on the 4.18.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.18.5. Users on the 4.22.x LTS releases stream should upgrade to 4.22.1. The asynchronous MDN destination is now constrained rather than taken verbatim from the inbound message.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Camel: affected 4.0.0 <4.18.5 (maven); affected 4.19.0 <4.22.1 (maven); unaffected 4.18.5 (maven); unaffected 4.22.1 (maven); unaffected 4.23.0 (maven)

### CVE-2026-80463 — Apache bRPC: Unbounded Memory Accumulation in Stream Message Reassembly
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Unbounded memory accumulation in the stream message reassembly path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows remote attackers to exhaust the memory of a server (denial of service) by sending an endless sequence of continuation data frames.

Root Cause:
The streaming RPC protocol bounds every single data frame by max_body_size, but a fragmented stream message accumulates continuation frames into one buffer (_pending_buf) without any limit on the accumulated size. A malicious peer that can open a stream can therefore keep sending continuation frames to make the receiver accumulate an arbitrarily large in-memory message. Since the default flow-control settings (socket_max_streams_unconsumed_bytes=0) do not throttle the sending rate, the receiver's memory grows until the process runs out of memory and crashes or becomes unavailable.

Affected Scenarios:
Services that accept streams from untrusted clients (for example using brpc::StreamAccept or brpc::StreamCreate with the built-in streaming protocol) are affected.


How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3489 


Note:
The fix limits the accumulated payload of a fragmented stream message to max_body_size (default 64MB). When the accumulated payload exceeds the limit, the pending fragments are released and the stream is closed with error EMSGSIZE. After applying the fix, legitimate fragmented stream messages larger than max_body_size will be rejected; you can adjust the gflag max_body_size to change the limit.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 0 <1.18.0 (semver)

Credits: Claude

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread/2pf15ojj0vr7rtx95677kgtl1mx3gdgb [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-81755 — Apache bRPC: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption via Excessive Streams in a Single RPC Request
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Uncontrolled resource consumption in the streaming RPC component of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) allows a remote attacker to exhaust server memory and cause denial of service by sending a single RPC request that declares an excessive number of streams.

Root Cause:
In the streaming RPC feature, a client can declare multiple streams in one RPC request by putting extra stream identifiers into the repeated field `stream_settings.extra_stream_ids` of the RPC meta. On the server side, `StreamAccept` creates one response stream for every stream identifier declared by the request, without limiting the number of streams accepted in a single RPC. The request body size is only bounded by `max_body_size` (default 64MB), which is enough to carry millions of stream identifiers. Each accepted stream allocates its own bthread execution queue and associated resources, so a single crafted request can make the server create a huge number of streams and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service.

Affected Scenarios:
Use a bRPC server that serves streaming RPC and calls `StreamAccept` to accept streams from untrusted clients.

How to Fix: 
(Choose one of the following options) 
1. Upgrade bRPC to the 1.18.0 version.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3493 


Note:
The fix adds a new gflag `stream_max_streams_per_request` with a default value of 64. Requests declaring more streams than the limit are rejected before any response stream is created. Applications that legitimately need to accept more than 64 streams in one RPC must raise this flag; otherwise such requests will fail after applying the fix.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 0 <1.18.0 (semver)

Credits: Claude

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread/2pf15ojj0vr7rtx95677kgtl1mx3gdgb [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-82210 — Apache bRPC: Remote denial of service (crash) via malformed stream feedback frames
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-617 CWE-617 Reachable Assertion
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Enforceable assertion in the streaming feature of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows a remote attacker to crash the server process by sending a malformed stream feedback frame.

Root Cause:
When handling FRAME_TYPE_FEEDBACK frames, bRPC calls Stream::SetRemoteConsumed() which contains CHECK(_cur_buf_size > 0) and unconditionally asserts CHECK(buf.IsEmpty()) on the frame payload. A feedback frame that carries an unexpected payload, or a feedback frame received on a stream where flow control is disabled (cur_buf_size == 0), reaches these assertions. On failure, CHECK failures abort the process, allowing an unauthenticated single client (once a stream is established) to terminate the server and cause a denial of service.

Affected Scenarios:
Use bRPC server with the streaming control feature (Stream API) served from untrusted network.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3494 

The fix rejects malformed feedback frames with EPROTO and closes only the affected stream instead of crashing the whole process, and it bounds buffer shrinking so cur_buf_size never drops to 0 while flow control is enabled.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 0 <1.18.0 (semver)

Credits: Claude

### CVE-2026-82230 — Apache bRPC: Stack Exhaustion via Unbounded Recursion in mcpack2pb Parser

Uncontrolled recursion in the mcpack2pb component in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows remote attackers to make the server crash via sending deeply nested mcpack data.

Root Cause:
The bRPC mcpack2pb parser (used to serve nshead_mcpack / ubrpc / public_pbrpc requests) recursively parses nested objects and arrays without any depth limit. For a protobuf message that references itself (e.g. a repeated message field), the generated parser recurses once per nesting level of the incoming mcpack object. A deeply nested request makes the recursion grow unbounded, overflow the stack and crash the process.

How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)

2. Apply this patch: https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3499

Note:
No matter which option you choose, you should know that the fix enforces the documented parsing depth limit MAX_DEPTH (128) on the parse path, the same limit the serializer already applies. If your requests contain mcpack messages nested deeper than 128 levels, the request will be failed after applying the fix.

- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 0 <1.18.0 (semver)

### CVE-2026-82231 — Apache bRPC: Malformed Thrift T_EXCEPTION reply causes process termination in Thrift client

A Thrift client in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0, built with WITH_THRIFT which is off by default) can be crashed by the server peer it talks to. When the server returns a T_EXCEPTION reply whose exception struct is malformed, the client decodes it without catching what Apache Thrift throws (TProtocolException, TTransportException or std::length_error). The exception unwinds out of the bthread task function and the process calls std::terminate(), terminating the whole process along with every other in-flight RPC.

This is the client response path, so the adversary is the server peer, which THREAT_MODEL.md treats as untrusted. It requires a WITH_THRIFT build (off by default).

### CVE-2026-82310 — Apache Airflow FAB provider: FAB auth manager: deactivated users retain and renew Core API JWT access
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-16 | Updated: 2026-09-17 | Max CVSS: 7.2
- CWE: CWE-613 CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Apache Airflow FAB provider: deactivating a user account does not stop tokens issued to that account before deactivation. Password authentication correctly rejects the disabled account, but the Core API continues to accept an existing, unexpired token naming it, and lets that token mint a replacement — so the account keeps its role-scoped access indefinitely after an administrator has disabled it. The user replays their own legitimate credential; no signature forgery or privilege escalation is involved, and the access stays within the roles the account already held.

Affects deployments using Airflow 3 with the FAB auth manager and Core API token authentication, where an administrator deactivates an account whose row remains in the database and whose previously issued token has not expired. The trigger is administrative deactivation as a containment action, which silently fails to contain.

Users of apache-airflow-providers-fab are recommended to upgrade to version 3.9.0 or later, which rejects tokens naming a deactivated account.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Airflow FAB provider: affected 2.0.0 <3.9.0 (semver)

Credits: Mayank Jangid (OpenSec); Jarek Potiuk

### CVE-2026-82311 — Apache Airflow FAB provider: FAB password reset never invalidates sessions: string/int _user_id comparison is always false
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-16 | Updated: 2026-09-17 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-613 CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Apache Airflow FAB provider: resetting a user's password does not delete that user's existing database-backed sessions, despite documented behaviour that it does. The cleanup compares the string identifier Flask-Login stores in the session against the user's integer database identifier, so the comparison never matches and no session is removed. An attacker who already holds a copy of the victim's session cookie keeps access as that user after the password change, so the reset does not evict them.

Affects deployments using the FAB auth manager with `[fab] session_backend=database`. The trigger is an administrator (or the user) running the supported password-reset command as a containment action after a session cookie has been compromised; the secure-cookie backend is out of scope, as it documents that it cannot centrally delete sessions.

apache-airflow-providers-fab 3.9.0 also fixes CVE-2026-86462, a second, independent route to the same outcome via the Admin user-edit endpoint; a single upgrade closes both.

Users of apache-airflow-providers-fab are recommended to upgrade to version 3.9.0 or later, which compares the identifiers consistently.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Airflow FAB provider: affected 2.4.2 <3.9.0 (semver)

Credits: Mayank Jangid (OpenSec); Jarek Potiuk

### CVE-2026-82331 — Apache BuildStream: tar source extraction escape
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-23 | Updated: 2026-09-23 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-59 CWE-59 Improper link resolution before file access ('link following')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') vulnerability in the `tar` source plugin of Apache BuildStream running on Python < 3.12 allows malicious source tarballs to write files on the host, with the privileges of the user running BuildStream, via symlinks as part of source fetching.
The impact of this issue is mitigated by:

* BuildStream projects should only use trusted sources in their elements as otherwise the build output can also not be trusted
* Tracking a source tarball pins its SHA256 hash, which prevents MITM attacks of users that are fetching an already tracked project
* When running on Python >= 3.12, BuildStream >= 2.3.0 already makes use of the Python `tarfile` filter functionality, which blocks the symlink escape

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.8.1, which fixes this issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache BuildStream: affected 0 <=2.8.0 (semver); unaffected 2.8.1 (semver)

Credits: Gjoko Krstic of Zero Science Lab

### CVE-2026-82375 — Apache Roller: Server-side request forgery via entry trackback and enclosure URLs
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-28 | Updated: 2026-11-16 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-918 CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:security@apache.org:Secondary): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:L`

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Apache Roller 6.1.5 allows an authenticated user with entry-editing rights on a weblog to cause outbound HTTP requests to attacker-chosen destinations through legacy outbound Trackback and entry enclosure handling. The Trackback control is hidden in the standard UI, but its action remains directly reachable; the enclosure path is relevant only when an author supplies an enclosure URL. ### CVE-2026-82425 — Apache bRPC: Reachable Assertion in Socket::OnInputEvent Allows Remote Denial of Service
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-617 CWE-617 Reachable Assertion
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

A reachable assertion in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows a malicious remote peer to crash the process, resulting in denial of service.

Root Cause:
When a Socket with health checking enabled fails, Socket::WaitAndReset closes its file descriptor while the event dispatcher may still be delivering an input event (EPOLLIN/EVFILT_READ) that was fetched for the just-closed fd. If the health check then succeeds and revives the Socket, Socket::Address succeeds again while the fd is still -1 (the next write reconnects on demand). In that window, Socket::OnInputEvent hits CHECK(!(events & EPOLLIN)) (or the kqueue equivalent) because the Socket is addressable but has no fd. CHECK failures terminate the process when bRPC is built with glog or when the gflag -crash_on_fatal_log is enabled (CHECK always terminates in OFFICIAL_BUILD/NDEBUG builds as well).

Affected Scenarios:
Applications using bRPC clients with health check enabled (-health_check_interval). A malicious remote peer that the client connects to can deliberately abort connections and immediately accept the health check probes, racing connection teardown against health check revival to trigger the assertion and abort the process.

How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3510 

Note:
After applying the fix, stale input events on a Socket revived without an fd are silently dropped instead of triggering the assertion. No user-visible interface or wire protocol is changed.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 0 <1.18.0 (semver)

Credits: condy0919

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread/2pf15ojj0vr7rtx95677kgtl1mx3gdgb [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-82427 — Apache Storm Nimbus: Path Traversal as the Supervisor User via Unsanitised Blobstore Map Local Name
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-22 CWE-22  Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

A topology's `topology.blobstore.map` lets the submitter choose a local name for each blob that the
supervisor localises. That name was used to build a path under the topology's working directory without
normalisation, in both `AsyncLocalizer` and `Container.createBlobstoreLinks`, and the symlink helper
force-deletes whatever already exists at the target before creating the link.

A submitter could therefore use `../` segments to direct that delete-and-symlink operation at an arbitrary
path, as the supervisor user, on every node the topology is scheduled onto. The consequences include
recursive deletion of supervisor-owned content and planting a symlink that causes a subsequent worker
launch to execute attacker-chosen code as another tenant's operating-system user, which defeats the
isolation that `supervisor.run.worker.as.user` is intended to provide.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the resolved target must lie inside the expected root at both call sites.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict topology submission to trusted principals, and may
reject submissions whose `topology.blobstore.map` entries contain path separators or `..` segments before
they reach Nimbus.

Credit

The ASF -- found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache Storm.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Storm Nimbus: affected 3.0.0 <3.1.0 (semver)

Credits: The ASF using Claude Agents

- https://lists.apache.org/thread/o0j51w6m0qdmwypvzfnd8w97s7ysnmyj [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-82428 — Apache Storm Client: Cross-Tenant Dependency Jar Substitution via Predictable Blob Keys
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-22 CWE-22  Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

Dependency artifacts uploaded with `storm jar --artifacts` were stored under a blob key derived only from
the Maven coordinate, for example `dep---.jar`. The key was therefore identical
for every user of the cluster and predictable in advance. When the blob already existed, the uploader
caught `KeyAlreadyExistsException` and silently reused it, with no check that the existing blob's content
or owner matched the artifact the submitter had resolved.

A user who uploaded a blob under such a key first therefore controlled the bytes that every later submitter
of the same coordinate would receive on the worker classpath, resulting in code execution inside another
tenant's topology.

This affects deployments where more than one principal may create blobs and where the `--artifacts`
dependency feature is used.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where each uploaded artifact receives a key carrying a freshly generated UUID and a
pre-existing blob is no longer silently reused.

Note that the corrected key generation is on the SUBMITTING CLIENT, so upgrading the cluster alone does not
close this; every client that runs `storm jar --artifacts` must also be upgraded. Operators should audit
existing `dep-` blobs for unexpected owners before upgrading. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should
avoid the `--artifacts` mechanism in multi-tenant clusters and distribute dependencies inside the topology
jar instead.

### CVE-2026-82429 — Apache Storm Worker Launcher: Local Privilege Escalation to Root via a Time-of-Check Race in the Worker Launcher
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-367 CWE-367 Time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

The setuid-root `worker-launcher` binary adjusts ownership and permissions of worker directories by walking
the tree with FTS and calling `lchown` and `chmod` on each entry's full pathname while running with an
effective uid of 0. Both syscalls re-resolve the path at the time of the call, after FTS has classified the
entry, and the trees being walked are owned and writable by the untrusted topology user.

A tenant running code on a supervisor node could therefore replace an intermediate directory component with
a symbolic link between classification and the privileged operation, redirecting the root-owned `lchown` or
`chmod` at an arbitrary file on the host. The operation is repeatable at will, since crashing a worker
forces a relaunch and blob updates re-run the walk, so a failed attempt costs the attacker nothing.

This crosses the boundary that `supervisor.run.worker.as.user` and container isolation are intended to
enforce. It is the same defect class as the Hadoop container-executor issues from which this code derives.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the privileged walk operates on file descriptors it has already stat'd rather than
on pathnames re-resolved at call time.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should not run untrusted topology code on supervisors configured with
`supervisor.run.worker.as.user`, since the launcher is the boundary being crossed. Note that the launcher
must be rebuilt and reinstalled after upgrading; replacing the Java artifacts alone is not sufficient.

### CVE-2026-82430 — Apache Storm Worker Launcher: Local Privilege Escalation to Root via Container Command Files Chowned to the Tenant
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-367 CWE-367 Time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

When launching a Docker or OCI worker, the setuid-root `worker-launcher` first changes ownership of the
entire worker directory to the untrusted topology user, and only afterwards reads and acts on the command
file that the supervisor wrote into that same directory. The file is opened without `O_NOFOLLOW` and without
re-verifying its owner, so between the ownership change and the read the tenant can replace its contents.

For the Docker path the parsed command is executed with real uid 0, and the command sanitiser is not a
privilege boundary: it admits `-v` with an arbitrary source, `--device`, `--cap-add`, `--security-opt`,
`--user` and `--net`, and copies positional arguments through verbatim. A rewritten file therefore yields an
attacker-authored, root-equivalent container invocation with the host filesystem available.

For the OCI path the same rewrite window applies, and mount validation is structural only, with no
source or destination allow-list, so arbitrary host paths can be bind-mounted read-write into the
container. The `username` field of the command file is likewise attacker-settable and is checked only
against non-root and minimum-uid rules, permitting execution as another tenant's uid.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the command file is validated before the ownership change and re-verified on open,
and where mount sources and destinations are constrained by configuration.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should disable Docker and OCI worker isolation, or restrict topology
submission on affected supervisors to trusted principals. Note that the launcher must be rebuilt and
reinstalled after upgrading.

### CVE-2026-82431 — Apache Storm Client: Authorization Bypass When nimbus.groups Is Configured Without nimbus.users
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Description

`SimpleACLAuthorizer` evaluated the user-level command set by returning early when `nimbus.users` was empty,
before `nimbus.groups` was considered. An operator who restricted cluster access by group alone, leaving
`nimbus.users` unset, therefore received no restriction at all: every authenticated principal was permitted
every user-level operation, including `submitTopology`, `beginFileUpload` and `getNimbusConf`.

`docs/SECURITY.md` presents `nimbus.groups` as a supported way to lock down a cluster, so a deployment
following the documentation could believe it was restricted while it was not. The failure is silent; nothing
in the logs or the configuration indicates that the group list is being ignored.

Both lists left empty continues to mean that no restriction is configured, which is the shipped default and
is unchanged.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where `nimbus.groups` is evaluated whether or not `nimbus.users` is set.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should additionally populate `nimbus.users` with the intended
principals, since a non-empty user list causes the group list to be evaluated on affected versions.
Operators should review Nimbus access logs for operations by principals outside the intended groups.

Note that after upgrading, a cluster configured with `nimbus.groups` alone becomes restrictive for the first
time. This includes `NimbusClient`, which calls `getLeader` on every connection, so clients outside the
configured groups will begin to be refused.

### CVE-2026-82432 — Apache Storm Nimbus: Blobstore Authorization Bypass via Rebalance Configuration Overrides
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-863 CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

Nimbus validated `topology.blobstore.map` against the calling subject at submission time only. The rebalance
operation accepts configuration overrides and stripped a small set of keys from them, but never re-ran that
validation, so a caller authorised to rebalance a topology could introduce a blobstore map entry naming a
blob whose ACL does not grant them access. Supervisors localise whatever key the map names, placing the
blob's contents into the topology's working directory.

The same advisory covers `listBlobs`, which performed no authorization check and passed no subject, unlike
the neighbouring `getBlobMeta` and `beginBlobDownload` operations. It therefore returned every key in the
blobstore to any caller able to reach the Nimbus Thrift port, which provides the key names that make the
above practical. On its own the disclosure is metadata only.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where rebalance configuration overrides are validated exactly as submission-time
configuration is, against the rebalancing caller, and where `listBlobs` applies the configured
authorization.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict rebalance rights to trusted principals, keeping in mind
that membership of a topology's `topology.users` or `topology.groups` confers them.

### CVE-2026-82434 — Apache Storm Nimbus, Apache Storm Client: Disclosure of the Topology ZooKeeper Credential to Read-Only Users and to Logs
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 10
- CWE: CWE-522 CWE-522 Insufficiently Protected Credentials; CWE-532 CWE-532 Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 10 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H`
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 6.5 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Description

When ZooKeeper authentication is configured, Storm deliberately retains
`storm.zookeeper.topology.auth.payload` in the topology configuration, because workers need it. Nimbus then
served that configuration verbatim to any caller holding read-only topology permissions, so a user whose
only grant was the ability to view a topology received its ZooKeeper credential.

That credential is not read-only. The cluster state implementation uses write-capable ACLs for worker
heartbeats, backpressure and error state, so a recipient can forge or remove that state for the topology
concerned. It is not a write credential on assignments.

The same advisory covers the submission client, which logged the generated payload at INFO on every
submission that generated one, and the SASL handlers, which logged it at DEBUG. The credential therefore
also reached any log aggregation or support bundle collected from the cluster.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the payload is removed from the configuration served to read-only callers and is no
longer written to logs.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should rotate `storm.zookeeper.topology.auth.payload` for existing
topologies, review retained logs and support bundles for the value, and restrict read-only topology
permissions to trusted principals.

The ASF -- found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache Storm.

### CVE-2026-82435 — Apache Storm Worker: Unauthenticated Remote Memory Exhaustion in the Worker Messaging Decoder
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-789 CWE-789 Memory allocation with excessive size value
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Description

The worker's Netty message decoder is installed ahead of the SASL authentication handlers in the pipeline
and acts on frames before any authentication has taken place. It allocated buffers sized from a
length field carried in the frame, so a single frame from an unauthenticated peer able to reach a worker
slot port could drive a large allocation.

`storm.messaging.netty.authentication` defaults to false, and the decoder runs before the handler that
enforces it in any case, so no credentials are required. The attacker needs only TCP reachability to a
worker port.

The effect of a single frame at the default 768 MB worker heap has not been measured to distinguish
sustained worker loss from transient garbage-collection pressure. The severity assigned to this advisory
reflects the more conservative reading; consumers who require a precise figure should test against their own
worker heap configuration.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where frames are decoded only after the handshake completes.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should ensure that worker slot ports are reachable only from within the
cluster, as the security model already recommends, and should enable
`storm.messaging.netty.authentication` where the deployment permits it.

### CVE-2026-82436 — Apache Storm Client: Deserialization of Untrusted Data from the State Store
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-09 | Updated: 2026-11-12 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of untrusted data
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

`DefaultStateSerializer`, used to persist and restore stateful bolt checkpoints, configured Kryo with class
registration disabled and an instantiation strategy that constructs objects without invoking their
constructors, then deserialized whatever bytes the state store returned. A party able to write to the
topology's keyspace in the state store, for example a co-tenant of a shared Redis instance or anyone with
network access to it, could therefore place a serialized object graph that executes code inside the worker
JVM when the state is restored.

This requires the Redis-backed state provider, which is not the default. Write access to a state-store key
is a data-plane privilege; code execution in the worker JVM is not, so the two are not equivalent.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the state serializer requires registered classes.

Note that this is a behaviour change for existing state: checkpoints written by an affected version may fail
to restore, and a migration step may be required. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict
network and credential access to the state store to the cluster itself.

### CVE-2026-82438 — Apache Storm Webapp: Authenticated API Responses Exposed to Arbitrary Web Origins
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-346 CWE-346 Origin Validation Error; CWE-942 CWE-942 Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Description

Three separate mechanisms allowed a web page on an unrelated origin to read responses that Storm's HTTP
components served to an authenticated user.

The Logviewer reflected the request's `Origin` header back in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` while also
sending `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. The published security model documents a permissive
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` posture as accepted, which is safe precisely because browsers refuse to
honour `*` together with credentials; reflecting the concrete origin removes that protection.

The shared CORS filter used by the UI, the Logviewer and DRPC was configured with a response header name
where an initialisation parameter name was expected. The container ignored the setting and applied its own
defaults, which allow credentials.

Finally, the UI and Logviewer wrapped API responses in a caller-supplied JSONP callback for every GET
request. A script element on any origin can load such a response, which bypasses the same-origin policy
entirely rather than negotiating it, and there was no way to turn the behaviour off.

In each case the effect is that a page visited by an authenticated operator can read cluster, topology and
log data on their behalf.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the Logviewer no longer reflects the request origin in a credentialed response, the
CORS filter is configured explicitly, and JSONP wrapping is governed by `ui.enable.jsonp`, which defaults to
false.

Note that disabling JSONP is a behaviour change for tooling that passes a `callback` query parameter; such
tooling should be moved to ordinary JSON requests.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should place the UI, Logviewer and DRPC HTTP endpoints behind a reverse
proxy that strips `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` from responses and
rejects requests carrying a `callback` parameter.

### CVE-2026-82439 — Apache Storm DRPC: Unauthenticated Unbounded Memory Growth in DRPC
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of resources without limits or throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Description

The DRPC server kept a map from function name to request queue and created an entry the first time a
function name was seen. No code path ever removed an entry: request cleanup removed the request from its
queue, and the shutdown path drained queues, but the queue object and its map entry remained for the life of
the process.

Function names come from the client and are not constrained to functions any topology has registered, so the
number of retained entries is bounded only by the number of distinct names an attacker chooses to send, and
each retained entry holds the name itself. `drpc.authorizer` is unset by default, so no credentials are
required to reach the endpoint.

The retained state is permanent rather than a transient load spike, so the effect accumulates until the DRPC
server exhausts its heap.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where a function's queue is removed once nothing is waiting in it.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should configure `drpc.authorizer` so that only trusted principals can
reach the DRPC endpoints, and should ensure the DRPC ports are not reachable from untrusted networks.

### CVE-2026-82440 — Apache Storm Nimbus: Submitter-Controlled Class Instantiation in Nimbus via a Fail-Open Scheduler Strategy Allowlist
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-09 | Updated: 2026-11-12 | Max CVSS: 8.1
- CWE: CWE-470 CWE-470 Use of Externally-Controlled input to select classes or code ('unsafe reflection')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Description

Nimbus instantiates the class named by a topology's `topology.scheduler.strategy` when scheduling it. The
allowlist intended to constrain that choice, `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist`, was treated as
"allow any class" when unset, and it had no entry in the shipped `defaults.yaml`, so unset was the shipped
state. An authenticated submitter could therefore cause Nimbus to instantiate any class on the Nimbus
classpath that has a no-argument constructor.

Storm's own production artifacts contain classes with side effects suitable for this: instantiating
`org.apache.storm.testing.InProcessZookeeper` starts a ZooKeeper server with its own threads and sockets
and nothing closes it, and `org.apache.storm.LocalCluster` behaves similarly. Repeated submissions
therefore consume threads, sockets and memory in the most privileged daemon in the cluster.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where an unset allowlist means the strategies shipped with Storm rather than any class.

Note that this is a behaviour change: a cluster running an out-of-tree scheduler strategy without an
explicit allowlist will have those topologies refused until the class is added to
`nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist`. The rejection message names the refused class and the
configuration key.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist` explicitly to
the strategies they intend to permit.

- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Storm Nimbus: affected 3.0.0 <3.1.0 (semver)

Credits: The ASF using Claude Agents

### CVE-2026-82441 — Apache Storm Nimbus: Cross-Tenant Blob Deletion and Cluster Denial of Service via Unvalidated Topology Dependency Keys
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-14 | Updated: 2026-09-14 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper input validation; CWE-639 CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Description

A submitted topology carries two lists of blobstore keys, `dependency_jars` and `dependency_artifacts`,
which the client fills in after uploading the corresponding blobs. Nimbus performed no validation of their
contents on the submission path, yet acts on them in two places.

During cleanup of a finished topology, Nimbus deletes the keys named in those lists, and the deletion is
performed as the Nimbus subject, for which the blobstore short-circuits its ACL check. A submitter who
listed a key belonging to another topology, such as its `-stormjar.jar`, could therefore cause
that blob to be deleted when their own topology was cleaned up.

Separately, on acquiring leadership a Nimbus compares the dependency keys of all active topologies against
the blobstore contents and surrenders leadership if any is missing. A single key that does not exist, on a
single active topology, therefore causes every Nimbus to acquire leadership, surrender it and requeue
indefinitely, leaving the cluster without a leader and unable to schedule, clean up or accept submissions.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where a submission is refused unless every entry in both lists is a dependency blob key
and exists in the blobstore.

Note that this validates new submissions only; a topology stored by an affected version with an invalid list
is unaffected by the upgrade. An operator whose cluster is failing to retain a leader should inspect the
Nimbus log for the dependency keys reported as missing and remove or resubmit the topology naming them.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict topology submission to trusted principals.

Credit

This issue was discovered by rzo1 while investigating an unrelated blobstore defect.

- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Storm Nimbus: affected 3.0.0 <3.1.0 (semver)

### CVE-2026-82617 — Apache OpenNLP, Apache OpenNLP: ReDoS / stack exhaustion in RegexNameFinderFactory built-in EMAIL and URL patterns
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-09-11 | Updated: 2026-09-11 | Max CVSS: 10
- CWE: CWE-1333 CWE-1333 Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 10 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

The two built-in name-finder patterns exposed by
opennlp.tools.namefind.RegexNameFinderFactory - DEFAULT_REGEX_NAME_FINDER.EMAIL
and DEFAULT_REGEX_NAME_FINDER.URL - contain ambiguous nested quantifiers. An
application that obtains these finders through
RegexNameFinderFactory.getDefaultRegexNameFinders(...) and then applies them to
untrusted text through RegexNameFinder.find(String[]) or RegexNameFinder.find(String)
can be driven into super-linear backtracking or into unbounded matcher recursion by a
small crafted input.





For the EMAIL pattern, a long run of local-part characters that is never followed by an
@ forces the matcher to re-scan to end-of-input from every starting offset. Cost grows
quadratically with input length: an input of approximately 32 KB consumes several seconds
of CPU in a single find() call and returns no match, and each doubling of the input
multiplies the cost roughly four-fold.





For the URL pattern, the query-string sub-expression nests a capturing repetition inside
an outer repetition. The JDK matcher recurses once per query token, so an input of
approximately 4 KB containing many &-separated tokens exhausts the thread stack and
causes java.lang.StackOverflowError to propagate out of find(), terminating the
calling thread. On a thread created with a smaller stack (for example -Xss512k, typical
of server worker pools) approximately 1 KB is sufficient.





In both cases an attacker who can supply text for analysis can convert a single request
into seconds to minutes of pinned CPU, or into an abrupt thread death, denying service to
the embedding application. No authentication, special configuration, or model file is
required beyond the application having selected one of the two built-in finders.





This issue affects Apache OpenNLP: from 2.0.0 through 2.5.11; from 3.0.0-M1 through
3.0.0-M5.









Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.5.12, or to 3.0.0-M6 for users tracking the
3.0.0 milestone line, which fix the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache OpenNLP: affected 3.0.0-M1 <3.0.0-M6 (semver)
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache OpenNLP: affected 2.0.0 <2.5.12 (semver)

### CVE-2026-82840 — Apache Wicket: The session id is renewed only on the first sign in, not on re-authentication
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-01 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 7.2
- CWE: CWE-384 CWE-384 Session Fixation
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.2 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Session fixation in Apache Wicket.

org.apache.wicket.authroles.authentication.AuthenticatedWebSession is the authentication base class of Wicket's role-based security module, and its signIn(String, String) method is the entry point through which an application authenticates a session. Renewing the container session id at that point is the standard defence against an attacker who has fixed a session id in a victim's browser, and Wicket provides that renewal as org.apache.wicket.Session#changeSessionId(), whose documentation directs callers to invoke it on login for exactly that reason.

AuthenticatedWebSession#signIn(String, String) calls it inside a guard that succeeds only on the first transition of the session's signed-in flag. The session id is therefore renewed when a session first signs in, and is not renewed when a session that is already signed in authenticates again. signIn(String, String) returns true either way, so neither the caller nor the application can tell that the renewal did not happen.

An application is affected where it authenticates through AuthenticatedWebSession, which AuthenticatedWebApplication requires and which the shipped UsernamePasswordPanel uses, and where a session that is already signed in can authenticate again: a step-up prompt before a sensitive action, an account switch, or simply a sign-in form that stays reachable once the user is signed in. Nothing in the module hides that form from a signed-in session. Reaching the defect also requires an attacker to place a session id of their choosing in the victim's browser. JSESSIONID is set by the servlet container rather than by Wicket, so that needs a position Wicket does not grant, such as control of a host under the same registrable domain or a container configured to carry the session id in the URL, and the planted session has to be one the attacker has already signed in on, because a session that is not yet signed in does have its id renewed by the victim's authentication. An authentication attempt that fails signs the session out and closes the window. Applications that renew the session id in their own code after a successful authentication are not affected.

As a workaround, renew the session id from the application's own code on every successful authentication, by calling Session#changeSessionId() at the end of the authenticate(String, String) implementation.

This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.18.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.23.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.9.0 through 10.11.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Wicket: affected 8.18.0 <=8.19.0 (semver); affected 9.23.0 <=9.24.0 (semver); affected 10.9.0 <=10.11.0 (semver)

Credits: Emond Papegaaij

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/q812kjb74x2pt6956w0pcmkc4wwj95l9 [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-82942 — Apache bRPC: Race Condition on the Shared Socket Input Buffer in the RDMA Transport Causes Remote Denial of Service
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-362 CWE-362 Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

A data race in the RDMA transport of Apache bRPC (versions < 1.18.0) allows a remote client to crash the server process (denial of service) when RDMA is enabled at build time and runtime.

Root Cause:
When a bRPC server negotiates RDMA with a client, the handshake completes on the TCP fd, but the server kept parsing that fd afterwards as if it were still an RPC channel. The TCP-fd input stream and the RDMA QP input stream (driven by CQ events) shared the same Socket::_read_buf, preferred_index and parsing_context without synchronization. In addition, CQ event processing could start while the handshake parsing was still in progress, and the handshake ACK phase could consume bytes belonging to the next protocol. A remote, unauthenticated client that has completed the RDMA handshake can send data on the TCP fd at the same time RDMA messages are being processed, corrupting the shared input buffer and parser state and crashing the server process (CWE-362, availability impact).

Affected Scenarios:
Use a bRPC server with RDMA support enabled (built with BRPC_WITH_RDMA and serving rdma:// / SOCKET_MODE_RDMA sockets) and accept connections from untrusted clients. Deployments without RDMA are not affected.

How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3505

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache bRPC: affected 0 <1.18.0 (semver)

Credits: bzs1118

References:
- https://github.com/apache/brpc/issues/3479
- https://lists.apache.org/thread/2pf15ojj0vr7rtx95677kgtl1mx3gdgb [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-82956 — Apache Wicket: XSS in AjaxNewWindowNotifyingBehavior via the client-supplied window name
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-01 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 7.6
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper neutralization of input during web page generation in Apache Wicket.

org.apache.wicket.ajax.AjaxNewWindowNotifyingBehavior notices that a page instance has been opened in a second browser window or tab. It asks the browser for the value of window.name, which reaches the server as the request parameter windowName, and remembers what the browser reported in a field of the behaviour. That field is part of the page's serialized state, so the remembered value stays in the page store for as long as the page instance does.

On every later render of that page instance the behaviour builds the precondition of its Ajax call by substituting the remembered value into a single-quoted JavaScript string literal, and Wicket writes that precondition into the page as raw JavaScript, because the precondition of an Ajax call listener is script supplied by the caller and is emitted without quoting or escaping. Nothing on that path escapes the value. The window name is client-supplied and Wicket applies no validation to it, so a remembered name containing a single quote ends the literal and the rest of it runs as script in the application's origin, every time that page instance is rendered.

An application is affected only where it has explicitly added AjaxNewWindowNotifyingBehavior to a component. No part of the framework installs the behaviour, so an application that does not use it is not affected. The name the behaviour generates for itself, when the browser reports no name at all, is a random UUID and is not client-supplied.

This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Wicket: affected 8.0.0 <=8.19.0 (semver); affected 9.0.0 <=9.24.0 (semver); affected 10.0.0 <=10.11.0 (semver)

### CVE-2026-83531 — Apache Camel: Camel-Dynamic-Router Control Endpoint Compiles Predicate Expressions Supplied by Control Messages
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-19 | Updated: 2026-10-20 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-94 CWE-94 Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection'); CWE-917 CWE-917 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement ('Expression Language Injection')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection'), Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement ('Expression Language Injection') vulnerability in Apache Camel.



This issue affects Apache Camel: from 4.4.0 before 4.18.5, from 4.19.0 before 4.22.1.



The dynamic-router-control endpoint, introduced in 4.4.0, lets routing participants manage Dynamic Router subscriptions by sending control messages. When it handled a subscribe or update request, DynamicRouterControlProducer took the subscription predicate and the name of the language used to compile it from the incoming message, either from the predicate and expressionLanguage fields of a DynamicRouterControlMessage body or from the CamelDynamicRouterPredicate and CamelDynamicRouterExpressionLanguage headers. DynamicRouterControlService then resolved that language from the CamelContext and compiled the expression into a Predicate, with no allow-list and no opt-in. The compiled predicate was added to the channel's rule base and evaluated against every exchange routed through the corresponding dynamic-router endpoint for as long as the subscription existed. A route that forwards messages from an external transport to the control endpoint, as shown in the component documentation for routing participants in other JVMs or applications, therefore let any actor able to send a message on that transport supply an expression of their choosing, which was evaluated with the privileges of the Camel process. Any expression language available on the classpath could be selected, including the simple language, which is always present and was the default on the header path, so removing optional expression languages from the classpath did not prevent the issue. Exploitation requires the ability to send a message on a transport whose route forwards it to a dynamic-router-control endpoint; no other authentication or user interaction is needed. Releases before 4.4.0 are not affected, because their control channel took predicate expressions only from the endpoint URI configured by the route author.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.1. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on those lines must move to a supported release. After upgrading, a control message that carries a predicate expression or an expression language is rejected unless the new allowPredicateFromMessage option is enabled on the dynamic-router-control endpoint; enable it only when every sender of control messages is trusted. For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, do not forward messages from untrusted or shared transports to a dynamic-router-control endpoint. Where control messages must cross such a transport, authenticate the sender and make sure the predicate and expression language of each subscription are set by the route rather than taken from the incoming message, for example by removing the CamelDynamicRouterPredicate and CamelDynamicRouterExpressionLanguage headers and clearing the predicate and expressionLanguage fields of a DynamicRouterControlMessage before it reaches the endpoint. Removing optional expression languages from the classpath is not a sufficient workaround. As defence in depth, restrict who can send to the transports that feed the control endpoint, and on 4.23.0 and 4.22.1 set the allowedSchemes option of the dynamic-router endpoint to limit which endpoints a subscription's destinationUri may name.

**workarounds:** For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately, do not forward messages from untrusted or shared transports to a dynamic-router-control endpoint. Where control messages must cross such a transport, authenticate the sender and make sure the predicate and expression language of each subscription are set by the route rather than taken from the incoming message, for example by removing the CamelDynamicRouterPredicate and CamelDynamicRouterExpressionLanguage headers and clearing the predicate and expressionLanguage fields of a DynamicRouterControlMessage before it reaches the endpoint. Removing optional expression languages from the classpath is not a sufficient workaround. As defence in depth, restrict who can send to the transports that feed the control endpoint, and on 4.23.0 and 4.22.1 set the allowedSchemes option of the dynamic-router endpoint to limit which endpoints a subscription's destinationUri may name.

**solutions:** Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.23.0, which fixes the issue. If users are on the 4.22.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.22.1. If users are on the 4.18.x releases stream, then they are suggested to upgrade to 4.18.5. The 4.14.x releases stream and earlier reached end of life before this issue was resolved and will not receive a fix, so deployments on those lines must move to a supported release. After upgrading, a control message that carries a predicate expression or an expression language is rejected unless the new allowPredicateFromMessage option is enabled on the dynamic-router-control endpoint; enable it only when every sender of control messages is trusted. A new allowPredicateFromMessage option on the dynamic-router-control endpoint, defaulting to false, now decides whether the subscription predicate and its expression language may be taken from a control message. When it is false, a subscribe or update request whose DynamicRouterControlMessage body or headers carry a predicate expression or an expression language is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException, and the predicate and expressionLanguage configured on the endpoint are used instead. The option is not mapped from any message header, and the toD optimisation keeps it on the endpoint URI, so only the route author can enable it. The header form of a control message now also falls back to the endpoint configuration for parameters the message does not carry, so a subscription can be declared entirely on a static endpoint URI. Subscriptions that reference a predicate bean from the registry, or that pass a Predicate instance in the message body, are unchanged. On 4.23.0 and 4.22.1 the option is additionally marked as an insecure:dev security option, so the security policy framework treats an endpoint that enables it as insecure, which fails by default when camel.main.profile is set to prod, and the dynamic-router endpoint gains an allowedSchemes option, unset by default, that restricts which endpoint schemes a subscription's destinationUri may use. The 4.18.5 release carries the allowPredicateFromMessage option only, because the security-option metadata and the recipient-list scheme allow-list that the other two releases build on are not present on that maintenance line.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Camel: affected 4.4.0 <4.18.5 (maven); affected 4.19.0 <4.22.1 (maven)

### CVE-2026-83539 — Apache Wicket: XSS in SmartLinkLabel and SmartLinkMultiLineLabel via a javascript: URL in the model data
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-01 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper neutralization of input during web page generation in Apache Wicket.

org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.SmartLinkLabel and org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.SmartLinkMultiLineLabel display a text value and turn any URL they find in it into a hyperlink. Both escape the model value and then hand the escaped text to org.apache.wicket.extensions.markup.html.basic.DefaultLinkParser, which searches it for anything of the form scheme://rest and wraps each match in an anchor whose href is the matched text, copied in as it is. The pattern accepts any scheme, and there is no list of permitted schemes anywhere on the path. A text value naming a scheme that executes script therefore becomes an anchor that executes it, in the application's origin and in the reader's own session, when the reader clicks the link. Rendering the page is not enough on its own; the link has to be activated. Escaping does not prevent this and is not the issue: the characters the payload needs are all valid in a URL and are ones that org.apache.wicket.util.string.Strings#escapeMarkup() leaves alone, and the value ends up in a URL rather than in element text, which is a context that escaping model data does not make safe.

An application is affected where it renders text it received through either of these two components. That is what they are for: they exist to linkify email addresses and web URLs found in the data an application is displaying, so untrusted input is the purpose of the feature rather than a misuse of it, and no unusual configuration is involved. No other component uses this parser, and an application that uses neither SmartLinkLabel nor SmartLinkMultiLineLabel is not affected.

On 9.x and 10.x the Content-Security-Policy Wicket sends by default admits script only from a source carrying a per-response nonce, and a URL whose scheme executes script cannot carry one, so that default policy stops the script from running. This is a property of the default policy and not of these components. An application that has weakened or disabled its Content-Security-Policy, for this or for any unrelated reason, is affected in full. Wicket 8.x has no Content-Security-Policy support at all and is affected as it stands.

This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users of Apache Wicket 7.x or older, which are no longer supported, should upgrade to a supported version. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Wicket: affected 8.0.0 <=8.19.0 (semver); affected 9.0.0 <=9.24.0 (semver); affected 10.0.0 <=10.11.0 (semver)

Credits: Emond Papegaaij
