### CVE-2026-107937 — Apache CXF: The attachment header size and count limits can be bypassed, which allows denial of service through memory exhaustion.
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-09 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

In Apache CXF, the parser for multipart/MTOM attachment part headers did not fully enforce the configured attachment-max-header-size (default 300 characters) and attachment-headers-max-count (default 500) limits. The size limit was applied only to each physical line, not to a header value built from continuation lines or to the combined values of a repeated header. The count limit was checked against the number of distinct header names, not the total number of header lines. A remote, unauthenticated attacker could send a multipart request with very large folded or repeated part headers. The server would then allocate memory without bound, causing a denial of service. 
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache CXF: affected 4.2.0 <4.2.4 (semver); affected 4.0.0 <4.1.9 (semver); affected 0 <3.6.13 (semver)

Credits: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects and independently by Mike Read (github.com/Michael-JRead)

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/x9twtpv3d04qj83t6w9xkh9y2q28zztj [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/09/12

### CVE-2026-107938 — Apache CXF: The Netty HTTP client transport does not perform TLS hostname verification.
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-09 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-297 CWE-297 Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

In Apache CXF, the Netty-based HTTP client transport (cxf-rt-transports-http-netty-client) did not verify that the hostname in the server’s TLS certificate matched the host being called. This applied over both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, even when disableCNCheck was left at its default value of false. The certificate chain was validated against the configured trust store, but the endpoint’s identity was not. A network attacker able to intercept traffic could present any certificate trusted by the client, such as a publicly issued certificate for a domain they control, and impersonate the target service. They could then read or modify the exchanged messages, including credentials. 
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache CXF: affected 4.2.0 <4.2.4 (semver); affected 4.0.0 <4.1.9 (semver); affected 0 <3.6.13 (semver)

Credits: This issue was found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects

### CVE-2026-108039 — Apache CXF: Prevent unbounded XML document size in StaxUtils by adding default element and character limits
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-09 | Updated: 2026-10-15 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-776 CWE-776 Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

By default, StaxUtils placed no limit on the total number of elements or the total number of characters in an XML document. A very large request could therefore use a lot of memory and CPU during parsing, especially where CXF builds a DOM from the input (for example SAAJ or WS-Security), and could cause a denial of service when no request size limit was configured. Both limits now have defaults: the maximum element count is 100 × maxChildElements (5,000,000 by default), and the maximum document size is 256M characters. Applications that process larger documents can raise the limits with the org.apache.cxf.stax.maxElementCount and org.apache.cxf.stax.maxXMLCharacters properties.
Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.4 or 4.1.9 or 3.6.13, which fix this issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache CXF: affected 4.2.0 <4.2.4 (semver); affected 4.0.0 <4.1.9 (semver); affected 0 <3.6.13 (semver)

Credits: Wanxin Yin (yaklang.io) <yhellow123456@gmail.com>

### CVE-2026-110985 — Apache Kafka: Broker silently skips JWT signature verification for SASL/OAUTHBEARER when the JWKS endpoint URL is not configured
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-05 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-345 CWE-345 Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity and its child; CWE-347 CWE-347 Improper verification of cryptographic signature; CWE-1287 CWE-1287 Improper validation of specified type of input; CWE-636 CWE-636 Failing Open
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

A Kafka broker using SASL/OAUTHBEARER with the default validator (sasl.oauthbearer.jwt.validator.class=DefaultJwtValidator) selects its implementation from configuration. When sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.url is set, the validator verifies the JWT signature. When that URL is unset (the default) and no verification key resolver is supplied, DefaultJwtValidator silently falls back to ClientJwtValidator, which does not verify the JWT signature, algorithm, or issuer - and the broker starts with no warning or error. This is the residual of CVE-2026-33557, whose fix restored signature verification only on the path where the JWKS endpoint URL is set.


Impact:

A broker in this state accepts any structurally valid JWT, including "alg":"none" tokens. An unauthenticated remote attacker who can reach the listener can forge a token asserting any principal - including configured superusers - and gain full access to the cluster. Only brokers that enable SASL/OAUTHBEARER validation without a JWKS endpoint URL (and without a custom verification key resolver) are affected; brokers that set the URL verify signatures and are not affected. Unlike CVE-2026-110952 (issuer/audience not enforced by default), here no signature is verified at all.


Mitigation (all affected versions, no upgrade required):

Set sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.url for every listener/mechanism that uses OAuthBearerValidatorCallbackHandler, or configure a signature-verifying sasl.oauthbearer.jwt.validator.class.

Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.1, and 4.4.0: a broker that would fall back to the non-verifying ClientJwtValidator fails to start with a ConfigException instead of running without signature verification (secure by default).

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 4.1.0 <=4.1.2 (semver); affected 4.2.0 <=4.2.1 (semver); affected 4.3.0 (semver)

Credits: San Zhang <falaxe1642@gmail.com>; Kaixuan Li <kaixuanli0131@gmail.com>; Evan Zhou <ezhou@confluent.io>

References:
- https://kafka.apache.org/cve-list [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-111089 — Apache Wicket: XSS via a resource bundle text written unescaped into generated JavaScript and markup
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-01 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 7.6
- CWE: CWE-79 CWE-79 Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.6 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Apache Wicket reads texts from the application's resource bundles — a localized label, a css class name — and writes some of them into the JavaScript and the markup it generates for a component. Those texts are placed inside single-quoted JavaScript string literals and inside quoted attribute values without being escaped for that context, so a text containing a quote ends the literal or the attribute, and what follows is parsed as script or as markup in the application's origin when the page loads.

A resource bundle entry is authored for the application and does not say where the framework will write it. The same key is read by the framework into element text, where Wicket escapes it, and into the contexts below, where it did not. A text containing an apostrophe, which is ordinary in several languages, is enough to break the page; a text under the influence of another party is enough to run script.

In org.apache.wicket:wicket-core, org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.upload.MultiFileUploadField writes the org.apache.wicket.mfu.delete message into a JavaScript string literal, and org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.Form writes the hidden-fields css class into the class attribute of the container it renders for its hidden fields; on 8.0.0 through 8.19.0 and 9.0.0 through 9.24.0 Form#appendDefaultButtonField writes the same css class into a second container. In org.apache.wicket:wicket-extensions, UploadProgressBar writes its UploadProgressBar.starting text into a JavaScript string literal, FilterForm writes the hidden-fields css class into the class attribute of its hidden input markup, and on 9.0.0 through 9.24.0 and 10.0.0 through 10.11.0 TrapFocusBehavior writes its current css class into a JavaScript string literal.

The Content-Security-Policy that Apache Wicket 9.x and 10.x send by default does not prevent the JavaScript cases: the generated script is written into a script element carrying the per-response nonce, so the injected code is part of a script the policy admits. It does prevent an inline event handler injected through the attribute cases.

This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 8.0.0 through 8.19.0, from 9.0.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.11.0. Users of Apache Wicket 7.x or older, which are no longer supported, should upgrade to a supported version. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Wicket: affected 8.0.0 <=8.19.0 (semver); affected 9.0.0 <=9.24.0 (semver); affected 10.0.0 <=10.11.0 (semver)

Credits: Pedro Santos

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/xyp4sm5mm7s618fktstb22577qxbmqw8 [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-111108 — Apache Kafka: Broker OutOfMemoryError via array allocation amplification in code-generated protocol readers
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-05 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of resources without limits or throttling; CWE-789 CWE-789 Memory allocation with excessive size value; CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Apache Kafka's code-generated protocol readers pre-size an array's collection from the element count declared by the sender. That count is checked only against the bytes remaining in the request buffer, which assumes about one byte per element; because most elements need several bytes, a request can declare far more elements than the buffer holds and still pass. For a keyed array the reader then allocates an ImplicitLinkedHashCollection of capacity (2 * count +1), so a request of a few tens of megabytes can force a heap allocation several times larger before any element is read. The pattern is emitted into every generated reader, so it affects all Kafka API types with an array field. 


Impact:

Request parsing happens before any authorization check. On a listener that does not require authentication (for example PLAINTEXT), an unauthenticated attacker can send a few concurrent requests that each declare a very large=

array length and allocate many times their wire size in broker heap, crashing the broker with an OutOfMemoryError. The reporter demonstrated three concurrent ~90 MB ProduceRequest (v3) connections exhausting a 1 GB heap (~8x amplification). On listeners that require authentication, the attacker needs valid credentials but no specific ACL, since parsing precedes authorization..


Mitigation:

Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. Until then, lowering socket.request.max.bytes and restricting network access to broker listeners reduces, but does not remove, exposure.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: generated readers cap the initial array pre-allocation at MessageUtil.MAX_PREALLOCATED_ARRAY_CAPACITY (1000) and grow it on demand, and reject a declared array length above MessageUtil.MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH (1,000,000).

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 3.3.0 <=4.1.2 (semver); affected 4.2.0 <=4.2.1 (semver); affected 4.3.0 <=4.3.1 (semver)

Credits: Mike Read (GitHub: Michael-JRead); Izzy Harker <iharker@confluent.io>; Alyssa Huang <ahuang@confluent.io>; Truc Nguyen  <trnguyen@confluent.io>

References:
- https://kafka.apache.org/cve-list [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/28/10

### CVE-2026-111115 — Apache Kafka: Broker OutOfMemoryError via tagged-field allocation amplification in flexible protocol request parsing
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-11 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Apache Kafka's code-generated readers for flexible protocol versions read a tagged-field count declared by the sender and retain a RawTaggedField object for each unknown field. That count was bounded only by the outer request frame size (socket.request.max.bytes); it was not checked against the remaining buffer bytes or capped. Because each entry can be encoded in as little as two bytes (unknown tag 0, size 0), a modest request can declare tens of millions of tagged fields and force one object allocation per declared field. Flexible request headers (header version 2, used by flexible APIs such as ApiVersions v3) are parsed this way, so the amplification applies to the request header itself.


Impact:
The flexible request header is parsed on the network thread before authorization, request dispatch, and request-time quota accounting. A client can send a request of a few tens of megabytes whose header declares about 20 million tagged fields, forcing roughly that many RawTaggedField allocations and exhausting broker heap or inducing process-wide GC stalls, denying broker service. Because the header is parsed for pre-authentication APIs such as ApiVersions (v3), the allocation can occur before authentication; no Kafka resource ACL or quota is required.

Mitigation:
Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. Until then, lowering socket.request.max.bytes and restricting network access to broker listeners reduces, but does not remove, exposure.

Resolution:
From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: generated readers bounds-check the tagged-field count for flexible-versioned messages, rejecting a negative count, a count exceeding the remaining buffer bytes, or a count exceeding a fixed maximum (10,000), before any per-field allocation.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 2.4.0 <=4.1.2 (semver); affected 4.2.0 <=4.2.1 (semver); affected 4.3.0 <=4.3.1 (semver)

Credits: Mufeed VH  <mufeed@winfunc.com>; Vivek R <vivek@winfunc.com>; Shay Elkin <selkin@confluent.io>

References:
- https://kafka.apache.org/cve-list [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/28/12

### CVE-2026-111496 — Apache Kafka: Kafka Streams StreamThread hang from integer overflow in stream-time punctuation
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-05 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-190 CWE-190 Integer overflow or wraparound; CWE-835 CWE-835 Loop with unreachable exit condition ('infinite loop')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Kafka Streams derives its stream-time clock from record timestamps. PunctuationSchedule.next() computed the next punctuation time as timestamp + (intervalsMissed + 1) * interval with no overflow check. A record with a timestamp at or near Long.MAX_VALUE advances stream time to that value, so the next stream-time punctuation overflows to a negative time. PunctuationQueue then re-queues that time and loops on it indefinitely while holding a lock, stalling the StreamThread.


Impact:

A single record is enough. The affected StreamThread stops processing, and because the record stays in the topic the hang returns on restart; an application whose partitions are all affected becomes unresponsive. Only the Streams application is affected, not the brokers or the cluster. Triggering it needs write access to a source topic whose topology uses stream-time punctuation, and a broker that stores the record: brokers from Apache Kafka 4.0.0 reject such a timestamp by default (log.message.timestamp.after.max.ms, one hour), so it is reachable only on older brokers or where that bound has been relaxed.


Mitigation:

Upgrade Kafka Streams to 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. As defense in depth, keep log.message.timestamp.after.max.ms bounded on source topics and restrict write access to them.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: the next punctuation time is computed with overflow-checked arithmetic (clamped to Long.MAX_VALUE), and a rescheduled punctuation is re-queued only when its time moves forward.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 1.1.0 <=4.1.2 (semver); affected 4.2.0 <=4.2.1 (semver); affected 4.3.0 <=4.3.1 (semver)

Credits: Mike Read (GitHub: Michael-JRead); Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>

References:
- https://kafka.apache.org/cve-list [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/28/14

### CVE-2026-111551 — Apache Kafka: Denial of service in Kafka Streams and client deserializers via unbounded memory allocation
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-05 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-789 CWE-789 Memory allocation with excessive size value; CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption; CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper input validation
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Several Kafka deserialization paths read a size or count field from input data and use it directly to allocate an array, collection, or byte buffer, with no check against the bytes actually available. A small crafted input can therefore declare a very large size and force a multi-gigabyte allocation. The affected paths are, in Kafka Streams, ProcessorRecordContext (header count), ChangedDeserializer (varint value length), CombinedKeySchema (foreign-key length, which could also produce a negative size), ProcessorMetadata (key length), and AssignmentInfo group-assignment decoding; and, in the clients library, ListDeserializer (used by ListSerde).


Impact:

An attacker can trigger the oversized allocation and raise an OutOfMemoryError that crashes the affected consumer or Kafka Streams thread; the broker and the rest of the cluster are unaffected. The reachable surface depends on the path: writing a crafted record to a Streams application's internal changelog or repartition topics, or committing crafted offset metadata to its consumer group (Streams internal paths); writing a crafted record to any topic that a consumer reads with ListSerde (ListDeserializer); or, as a member of a Streams consumer group, returning crafted assignment data when elected leader (AssignmentInfo). Because a crafted record remains in its topic, the error can recur on restart. The record size limit (max.message.bytes) does not help, because the allocation is driven by a size field rather than by the input's length.


Mitigation:

Upgrade to Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, or 4.4.0. Where authorization is enabled, restrict write access to each application's internal topics and consumer group to its own principal, and restrict who can produce to topics that are consumed with ListSerde.


Resolution:

From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0: these deserialization paths validate the declared size against the remaining input before allocating and reject input that fails the check.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 0.10.0.0 <=4.1.2 (semver); affected 4.2.0 <=4.2.1 (semver); affected 4.3.0 <=4.3.1 (semver)
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 0.10.0.0 <=4.1.2 (semver); affected 4.2.0 <=4.2.1 (semver); affected 4.3.0 <=4.3.1 (semver)

Credits: Peyton Kennedy <pkennedy@endor.ai>; Bartlomiej Dmitruk <bartek@striga.ai>; Mike Read (GitHub: Michael-JRead); Matthias J. Sax <matthias@confluent.io>; Lucy Liu <lucliu@confluent.io>

- CWE: CWE-444 CWE-444 Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests

- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Apache Traffic Server forwarded a malformed 302 response that should have been rejected as a parse error, because the Transfer-Encoding: chunked carve-out bypassed the rejection path. A response that two peers can read differently is then stored and served, allowing cache poisoning and response-framing desync.



This issue affects Apache Traffic Server: from 8.0.0 through 8.1.11, from 9.0.0 through 9.2.15, from 10.0.0 through 10.1.4, 10.2.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.2.16, 10.1.5, or 10.2.1, which fix the issue.

### CVE-2026-113508 — Apache Airflow: Logout token revocation fails open; errors silently swallowed
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-09 | Updated: 2026-11-12 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-613 CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Apache Airflow's logout endpoint attempted to revoke the presented token on the server, but any failure during revocation was silently ignored and logout still reported success. When the auth manager redirects logout to an external logout URL (for example the FAB or Keycloak auth managers), server-side revocation is the only thing that invalidates the Airflow token; it failed on database errors and, reliably, for tokens from an external issuer accepted via `[api_auth] trusted_jwks_url` whose token identifier is longer than 32 characters. Anyone holding a copy of a user's token from before logout could keep using it against the Airflow API until it expired. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Airflow: affected 0 <3.4.0 (semver)

Credits: Claude Security Scans; Pierre Jeambrun; Jarek Potiuk

References:
- https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/73562 [patch]
- https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/73788 [patch]
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/6t892ozodb9f3498jrsc8k0crbdnm7no [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/11/09/20

The Contact Form 7 WordPress plugin before 6.2.4 does not validate the type or extension of files uploaded through a form file field, and a flaw in its temporary-file cleanup leaves the uploaded file on disk, allowing unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files to the site. ### CVE-2026-115448 — Apache ZooKeeper: Unbounded recursion in snapshot serialization allows a client to render the server unrecoverable
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-04 | Updated: 2026-11-06 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770 Allocation of resources without limits or throttling
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Uncontrolled recursion in Apache ZooKeeper. The server serializes its data tree to a snapshot by recursing one stack frame per znode level, with no depth bound. A client permitted to create znodes (the default root ACL is open) can build a chain of nested znodes deep enough that taking a snapshot exhausts the JVM stack and kills the snapshot thread; sizes stay within jute.maxbuffer, so existing limits do not prevent it. This is a denial of service that becomes persistent: on restart the server rebuilds the deep tree from its transaction log and fails again while taking the startup snapshot, so it does not return to service, and recovery can entail data loss. The same log affects a leader and its followers, so it can spread across an ensemble.

This issue affects Apache ZooKeeper 3.8.0 through 3.8.7 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to 3.8.8 or 3.9.7, which fix the issue. As a workaround, use ACLs and authentication to restrict znode creation rather than relying on the default open root ACL.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache ZooKeeper: affected 3.9.0 <=3.9.6 (maven); affected 3.8.0 <=3.8.7 (maven)

Credits: Sai Sreewathsa Kovalluri, Shon Babu, and Kannan K of Innspark Solutions (https://innspark.in/); Prasath Jayasundar & PayPal Cyber Security Team

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/p892jm8qw0zqv8z152lpokyt7mp6gc41 [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/11/03/13

### CVE-2026-115644 — Apache Kafka: Connect Admin REST API Authentication Bypass via Unapplied REST Extensions
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-10-28 | Updated: 2026-11-05 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-288 CWE-288 Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Apache Kafka Connect contains an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting the admin REST API when admin.listeners is configured with a separate listener from the main listeners property.

When operators isolate the admin REST API by explicitly configuring the "admin.listeners" property, REST extensions specified via rest.extension.classes (such as BasicAuthSecurityRestExtension) are not registered or applied to the admin resource configuration.

While the primary REST API listener (configured via listeners) enforces configured authentication and authorization filters, endpoints mounted under the separate admin listener (/admin/loggers) fail to inherit or instantiate these extension filters. As a result, the admin logger endpoint accepts unauthenticated read and write requests even when security extensions are active on the main listener.

Impact:

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to the admin listener can:

  1. Read the complete set of logger names and levels, disclosing loaded class names and which security extensions are in use.
  2. Write logger levels, including with scope=cluster which propagates the change to all workers in the Connect cluster. This can be used to suppress
     logging (setting root to OFF) or generate excessive log output (setting root to TRACE), potentially impacting availability and observability.

Mitigation:

  Users who cannot upgrade immediately can remove the admin.listeners configuration (or leave it unset). When unset, admin resources share the regular listener and inherit its security extensions.

Resolution:


From Apache Kafka 4.2.2, 4.3.2, and 4.4.0, we make sure the REST extensions specified via "rest.extension.classes" will also apply to "admin.listeners".

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Kafka: affected 2.4.0 <4.2.2 (semver); affected 4.3.0 <4.3.2 (semver)

Credits: Bartłomiej Dmitruk <bartek@striga.ai>, Striga; Mickael Maison <mickael.maison@gmail.com>

References:
- https://kafka.apache.org/cve-list [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/28/15

### CVE-2026-115690 — Apache WSS4J: Replay protection bypassed by concurrent copies of a message
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-16 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-367 CWE-367 Time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default. The value is now checked and remembered in a single atomic step. Custom ReplayCache implementations should override the new ReplayCache.addIfAbsent method with an operation that is atomic in their underlying store. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.3 or 3.0.7 or 2.4.5, which fix this issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache WSS4J: affected 4.0.0 <4.0.3 (semver); affected 3.0.0 <3.0.7 (semver); affected 0 <2.4.5 (semver)

Credits: This issue was reported independently by Wanxin Yin (MegaVector / yaklang.io) and hataehoon (GitHub: @dpfkdlemtp).

Apache Commons Codec's Blake3 class documented the output of its doFinalize methods as depending on any previously finalized bytes, so that consecutive calls would return different output. In fact, doFinalize does not change the hash state: calling it again without supplying more input returns the same bytes. The key-derivation example in the class Javadoc, shipped since 1.16.0, derives two keys with two consecutive doFinalize calls. Code that follows it gets identical keys, so the separation between the derived keys is lost. The same applies to any application that calls doFinalize more than once on one instance and expects new output each time.



This issue affects Apache Commons Codec from 1.16.0 before 1.23.0.



Version 1.23.0 corrects the documentation, but the behavior of doFinalize is unchanged. Upgrading alone does not fix affected code. Users should check their applications for repeated doFinalize calls on the same Blake3 instance and derive multiple keys by requesting the combined length in one call and splitting the output, as the updated Javadoc shows.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Commons Codec: affected 1.16.0 <1.23.0 (maven)

Credits: Claude Security; Gary D. Gregory

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/ol71kdgopfxwlxgqmkd0jrfcw05wdq5z [vendor-advisory]
- http://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/11/09/29

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. An unauthenticated caller could supply a non-anonymous WS-Addressing wsa:ReplyTo or wsa:FaultTo address, and Axis2 would open a connection to that address to deliver the response or fault, allowing requests to internal hosts and delivery of response content to a host of the caller's choosing. ### CVE-2026-124023 — Apache Axis2/C: Out-of-bounds read in the Guththila XML reader wrapper
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-12 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds read
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the Guththila XML parser wrapper of Apache Axis2/C. On some malformed XML input the Guththila parser returned a raw input byte in place of an event code, and the AXIOM reader wrapper used that value as an index into a ten-entry lookup table without checking its range, reading heap memory past the end of the table. An unauthenticated client could trigger this by sending a crafted XML request to a server built with Guththila, the default parser, causing the request to be parsed incorrectly or, in some cases, the process to crash. The memory read is not returned to the client. This issue affects Apache Axis2/C: through 2.0.0. The fix is available in commits 23110287924e79d05a5b4712298c355d1f05c606 and f01683ec10e8fddb87279ec9351b3239021223e6 and will be included in the next release.

Affected:

### CVE-2026-124680 — Apache APISIX: Route-level authentication bypass via path normalization mismatch between routing and upstream forwarding
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-13 | Updated: 2026-11-13 | Max CVSS: 7
- CWE: CWE-436 CWE-436 Interpretation Conflict, resulting in CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization)
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Interpretation Conflict, resulting in (Incorrect Authorization) vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



An unauthenticated client can reach upstream paths protected
by a route-level auth plugin when a route without auth exists on the
same upstream and the upstream does not collapse encoded dot segments.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 0.9 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache APISIX: affected 0.9 <=3.19.0 (semver)

### CVE-2026-128841 — Apache Griffin Web Service: REST API is unauthenticated
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-16 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-306 CWE-306 Missing authentication for critical function
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in Apache Griffin Web Service. The REST API does not have any authentication. This includes sensitive endpoints, such as job submission when a Livy/Spark backend is configured. The API must be properly secured on the network level, and this fact was arguably not documented as clearly as it could have.



This issue affects Apache Griffin Web Service: all versions.



As this project is retired, we do not plan to release a version that fixes this issue. Users are recommended to find an alternative or restrict access to the instance to trusted users.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

### CVE-2026-129349 — Apache Shiro: DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-15 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 9.1
- CWE: CWE-287 CWE-287 Improper Authentication
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.1 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/S:N/AU:Y/R:U/V:C/RE:L/U:Red`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Shiro: affected 0 <3.0.1 (semver)

Credits: Joshua Rogers; Lenny Primak <lenny@flowlogix.com>

References:
- https://lists.apache.org/thread.html/1whn52ht402lhc782c3s843c9hho8b4y [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-129448 — Apache Roller: Unauthenticated deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint (releases before 6.1.5)
- Assigner: apache | Published: 2026-11-17 | Updated: 2026-11-17 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-502 CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

Affected:
- Apache Software Foundation / Apache Roller: affected 4.0.0 <6.1.5 (semver)

Credits: n0mi1k; Matt Raible
